title: A border colour sits with the other colours
goal: Colours have one home in the panel now, with one exception: the colour of a layer border is still a small swatch buried in the effects, and clicking it opens the system colour window instead of the app own picker. It should be a row in the Colour section like the rest, so it can be set on everything you picked and can wear a colour you saved.
notes: ColorSlot (PhotonzCore/ColorStyles.swift:24) has fill, stroke and text; the layer style border colour is not one of them, so it stayed behind as a raw SwiftUI ColorPicker in EffectsInspector.borderColorPicker (LayersPanel.swift, around line 1490) and opens the system panel, which is the one-undo-step-per-drag-tick problem the Color section already solved. Adding a slot means a case in ColorSlot with styleRole .ink, and Layer.colorSlots / colorHex(for:) / startingColorHex answering for it. Decide what a border colour row means on a layer whose border width is zero: the honest reading is that the row appears with the rest and setting it is harmless, but the alternative of only offering it above zero width is worth a line in the audit either way. Evidence: the Color one-home work (queue/audits/2026-09-03-color-one-home.json) moved every other colour and left this one, visible in queue/audits/2026-09-03-auto-layout-2.png where Effects still carries a colour control.
acceptance: The border colour is a row in the Color section, using the same picker the other colour rows use
It can be set on several picked layers at once and reads as mixed where they differ
A saved colour can be put on it, and editing that saved colour repaints every border wearing it in one step
The swatch in the effects is gone and nothing else in that section moved
An old document opens with its border colours unchanged
Try it: draw two boxes, give them a border, pick both and set the border colour once, then save it under a name
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
